column1: # The non-chorale part of the corpus: one row per work, tab-separated.
# Bach's chorales are generated — there are 413 of them and music21 ships a BWV
# index — so they are not listed here. Everything else is, because music21's
# MusicXML carries no usable title, opus or date: `work-title` is the filename
# where it exists at all. This table is therefore the curation, not a patch on
# top of one, and a corpus path that is not in it is skipped rather than guessed.
# Later sources will invert that. Humdrum kern carries !!!COM, !!!OTL and !!!ODT,
# and OpenScore ships composers.tsv, so their catalogues will be derived and this
# `composer` is resolved through tools/composers.tsv and may be any name that
# table knows; an unknown one is an error, not a new composer.
# The three metadata columns each do one job, which is why there are three of
#   genre       what kind of piece it is, from the vocabulary in composers.py
#   collection  the parent work or set — the third level of the browse, so
#               "Winterreise" gathers its songs and "String Quartet, Op. 18 no. 1"
#               its movements. Empty for a piece that stands alone.
#   catNo       the catalogue identifier, printed but never grouped on.
# A movement's character name belongs in the title, after an em dash.
# `year` is the year of composition, not publication. `tempo` is a playback speed
# in quarter-notes per minute chosen for listening — it is deliberately not the
# composer's metronome mark, which the engraving prints where one exists.
